title: Contact priority profiles and safelist behaviors (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working proposal for two related UX primitives in the Console: (1) Contact Priority Profiles — a way for tenants to define reusable oncall/contact policies (priority buckets, escalation rules, quiet hours) and (2) Contact Safelists — a mechanism to opt specific contacts or channels into bypassing certain throttles/noise-suppression behaviors.

Why this exists (background):
- Current routing UI mixes ad-hoc contact config per alert policy with tenant-level preferences. That makes reuse hard and encourages duplication.
- SRE and Platform teams have asked for a tenant-wide place to declare "how our people want to be paged" independent of SLO/alert definitions.
- Some customers run aggressive noise suppression (signal throttles, dedupe). They also have critical contacts who must always get high-fidelity delivery (pager duty primary escalation, pager bridge). We need a safe way to express exceptions.

Problems to solve / constraints:
- Keep per-policy authoring simple; non-owners should be able to select a profile rather than hand-craft the entire contact topology.
- Preserve safety: safelists must not be a way to circumvent billing/quotas or to disable throttling globally without audit.
- Support multi-channel contacts (email/sms/pager/teams webhook) and composite oncall objects (rotation-based PD, static user list).
- Make auditability obvious: who created profile, who enabled safelist, and when.
- UX must scale to orgs with 50+ profiles and many teams.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Create a Profiles gallery + editor that allows admins and team leads to define contact behaviors once and reuse them in Alert Policies and SLO-derived alerts.
- Allow admins to mark specific contacts/channels as Safelisted for a tenant or for a specific workspace or route.
- Provide clear warnings when safelisted contacts may increase alert noise or cost.
- Expose metrics / logs for safelist usage and delivery success in the Console (Deliverability dashboards).

Personas:
- Platform Admin (Alex): wants tenant defaults and can create profiles across teams.
- Team Oncall Lead (Priya): picks profiles for policy ownership and tweaks escalation windows.
- Incident Responder (Jordan): needs guaranteed reachability for certain channels during P1s.
- Product Owner (Luc): wants delegation but not the ability to bypass throttles.

Proposed UX components (high level):
1) Profiles Gallery (List view)
   - Primary columns: Name, Owner Team, Type (rotational/static), Active Policies count, Last modified, Safelist status (on/off).
   - Actions per row: Preview, Edit, Duplicate, Assign to policies, Audit history.
   - Filters: team, safelist-enabled, channel-type, owning-admin.
   - Quick create CTA (+New Profile) opens modal editor.

2) Profile Editor (modal / full-screen)
   - Basic info: name, description, owner team, visibility (tenant / workspace / private).
   - Contact composition: add rotation (PD integration), add static users, add contact channels (email/sms/webhook). Each contact has delivery preferences: primary delay, escalation delay, retry policy.
   - Priority presets: Critical / High / Normal with suggested timings. Users can save custom presets.
   - Bindings: preview which alert policies reference this profile (live).
   - Save with validation: warn on missing escalation path or no-mailback channel.

3) Safelist manager (separate tab / secondary modal)
   - Two scoped namespaces: Tenant-level safelist and Policy-level safelist.
   - Entry types: Individual contact (email/phone), Rotation (PD schedule ID), Channel (webhook id).
   - For each entry: reason, expiration (optional), created-by, created-at, linked-policy (optional).
   - Controls: enable/disable, schedule expiry, require two-step confirmation for tenant-wide safelists.
   - Visual indicator when a policy references a safelisted contact: small badge next to contact in policy editor.

4) Policy authoring integration (in Alert Policy screen)
   - Instead of "Add contact" show "Attach profile" and a smaller action "Override contacts".
   - If attach profile has safelisted members, show a warning tooltip: "This profile contains safelisted contacts that will bypass throttles. Confirm to attach."
   - Allow one-off temporary safelist for an individual policy (duration-limited).

Wireframe notes (screens / interactions):
- Gallery: two-column layout. Left: list/filter. Right: preview panel showing contact graph and recent delivery rate.
- Profile preview: timeline view (who gets paged at T+0, T+90s, T+5m). Hover each node to see last 30-day success rate.
- Safelist manager: table with inline expiration edit and an activity stream. Provide an "example" row that shows how a contact would behave under throttling vs safelisted.

Edge cases and behavior rules:
- If a profile references a rotation that becomes empty (no oncall), the policy should fallback to secondary contacts and flag an error in the policy health indicator.
- Safelisting a channel that is currently disabled by global admin should not re-enable it silently. Safelist only flags bypass of suppression, not global disablement.
- Billing notice: when a safelisted contact causes additional SMS pages beyond the tenant's normal volume, generate a post-fact billing alert and show cost-estimate in preview.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create/edit/delete reusable profiles and attach to alert policies.
- Tenant-level safelist support with audit trail and expiry.
- Policy editor warns when attaching profiles with safelisted members.
- Basic gallery filters and preview panel.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Scope of safelist (tenant vs workspace vs project). Proposal: default tenant-level, but allow workspace-limited entries. Need policy from security on who can create tenant safelists.
- Two-step confirmation UX for tenant safelists: require a second admin to approve? Or use an elevated permission + audit log?
- How to surface cost impact without spamming product UX? (heatmap vs one-line estimate).
- Interaction with existing signal-throttling: should safelist bypass all throttles or only dedupe and grouped suppression?

Metrics and telemetry to capture:
- Number of safelist entries and churn rate.
- Percentage of alerts that reached safelisted vs non-safelisted contacts.
- Delivery success/failure delta attributable to safelist.

Next steps / sprint plan (rough):
- Week 1: Align on scope with Security and Billing (owners: Maya + Hector).
- Week 2: Low-fidelity mocks (console team) + usability quick test with two customers (oncall leads).
- Week 3: Backend contract PR (notification-service) and public API changes for profile objects.
- Week 4: Implement gallery + editor flow (frontend) + integr. tests.
- Week 5: Safelist audit page + billing hooks + internal dogfood.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally opinionated around reusable profiles to reduce policy duplication. If we keep per-policy full contact editing, we lose the manageability benefit.
- Security: suggest "safelist create" be a gated permission. Put a strong audit surface on the action (why, who, expiration).

Quick sketch links (work in progress):
- UX sketches: drive:sketches/contact-profiles-2025-11.png
- PD integration notes: confluence:PD-INTEG-45

Comments / TODOs inline:
- [MAYA] confirm PD rotation representation (ID vs alias) and how to surface oncall owner.
- [HECTOR] validate billing event shape for extra SMS, add sample webhook.
- [SAMIR] work with infra to ensure safelist check is fast path in runtime (avoid tokenization cost per-message).

End of draft.
